tts.text: A patient presented with the showing skin rash (erythema multiforme). He has history of pneumonia 1 week ago. For which, he received treatment and the child has no symptoms now other that this skin rash. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism? Option A. Herpes simplex virus (HSV). Option B. Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Option C. Varicella. Option D. Measles.

image.captionAr: صورة السؤال الأصلية من الملف المرفوع؛ ليست تشخيصًا معتمدًا.
image.captionEn: Original source image for this question.

scenarioAr: طفل تعافى من pneumonia قبل أسبوع وبقي لديه الطفح المصوّر؛ المطلوب الميكروب الأرجح.
explanationAr: المفتاح B: Mycoplasma pneumoniae. شرح المصدر يربط الطفح الذي يسميه erythema multiforme بمرض تنفسي سبقه cough وcongestion وlow-grade fever. هذه التفاصيل الإضافية واردة في الشرح المرجعي وليست كلها في الـstem. حُفظ التصنيف كما ورد ولم يُستبدل تلقائيًا بتسمية أحدث.
incorrectOptionsAr: A: لم يختَر المصدر HSV رغم كونه ضمن الخيارات؛ قرينة الترجيح التي يذكرها هي المرض التنفسي السابق. C وD: لا يناقش المصدر استبعادهما تفصيليًا، فلا نختلق تاريخ تطعيم أوعلامات غير واردة.
clinicalPearl: The source links an erythema-multiforme-labelled eruption after pneumonia to Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
sourceExplanationEn:
The boy described in the vignette has facial swelling and a rash consistent with erythema multiforme that 
developed shortly after the onset of an illness characterized by nonproductive cough and congestion with 
low-grade fever. The most likely cause of the se findings is infection due to Mycoplasma pneumoniae. 
Mycoplasma is a common cause of upper respiratory tract infection and bronchitis in school-aged children. 

The fever associated with Mycoplasma infection is usually low grade, and the cough is nonproductive. 
Otitis media, pharyngitis, malaise, and headache also can occur. [Question 73 in PREP 2014]

scenarioAr: طفل لديه fever وآفة إصبع مصوّرة يسميها النص herpetic whitlow؛ المطلوب تصنيف العامل المسبب.
explanationAr: المصدر يختار A: DNA virus. يشرح أن HSV قد يُلقّح عبر break in the skin barrier ويسبب herpetic whitlow مع قابلية النكس. الرسم الموجود في الشرح يصنف Herpesviruses تحت enveloped double-stranded DNA viruses؛ هذا الرسم يظهر بعد الإجابة فقط.
incorrectOptionsAr: B: يخالف تصنيف HSV كـDNA virus في الرسم. C وD: كلاهما تصنيف bacteria، بينما المسبب المحدد في شرح المصدر HSV.
clinicalPearl: The source classification diagram places herpesviruses among double-stranded DNA viruses.
sourceExplanationEn:
HSV infection of the finger, known as herpetic whitlow, can occur by inoculation of the virus through a 
break in the skin barrier. Untreated, these infections gradually heal over two to three weeks, but similar to 
oral HSV-1 infection, they can recur. [UpToDate]

tts.text: A child presented with painful lesions on tongue, lips, and gingivae. What is the most likely diagnosis Option A. Herpangina. Option B. Herpetic gingivostomatitis.

scenarioAr: طفل لديه آفات مؤلمة على tongue وlips وgingivae؛ المطلوب التشخيص.
explanationAr: المفتاح B: Herpetic gingivostomatitis. يذكر الشرح vesicles مؤلمة تتحول إلى shallow ulcers مع gingivae ملتهبة قابلة للنزف وآفات حول الفم. ضعف تناول السوائل قد يؤدي إلى dehydration؛ لا يكفي التركيز على الطفح وإهمال الترطيب.
incorrectOptionsAr: A: المصدر يختار gingivostomatitis اعتمادًا على توزيع الآفات وإصابة اللثة، لكنه لا يقدم في هذه الفقرة وصفًا مقارنًا كاملًا لـherpangina؛ لا نضيف علامات غير موجودة في السؤال.
clinicalPearl: Painful gingival and oral lesions may lead to poor intake and dehydration in the source explanation.
sourceExplanationEn:
The boy in the vignette exhibits the common features of primary herpetic gingivostomatitis. This condition 
presents most often in children younger than 5 years of age, though it may occur at any age with the first 
bout of herpes simplex virus. On physical examination, numerous small  vesicles on an erythematous base 
will be noted  on the anterior palate, tongue, buccal mucosa, and gingivae. These lesions are painful and 
evolve into shallow ulcers. The gingivae may be erythematous, inflamed, and friable. Perioral lesions on 
the lips and nearby cheeks or chin may be present as well. The enanthem frequently follows several days 
of high fever, irritability, and malaise. As the lesions progress, many patients develop poor oral intake, 
drooling, and foul-smelling breath; some may be quite ill-appearing and are at risk for dehydration. Herpetic 
gingivostomatitis is self-limited and will resolve in 1 to 2 weeks. [Question 195 in PREP 2017]

image.captionEn: Original source question image; independent clinical review pending.

scenarioAr: طفل يتألم عند تنظيف الأسنان؛ ذُكرت صورة stomatitis محتملة وسُئل عن التدبير.
explanationAr: المفتاح مطبوع B? أي غير جازم، ثم ينص الشرح على عدم اقتراح magic mouthwash بصورة روتينية لقلة دليل الفائدة واحتمال الضرر وصعوبة التطبيق عند الصغار. التشخيص نفسه مسبوق بعلامة استفهام، ولا توجد الصورة المذكورة فعليًا في صفحة 642. بقي السؤال conflicting، ولم تُعتمد B كعلاج موثّق.
incorrectOptionsAr: A: لا يوجد تشخيص مثبت لنقص iron في السؤال. C: لا يذكر المصدر candidiasis. B: يتعارض اعتماده الروتيني مع شرح المصدر نفسه. لا تمثل هذه الخيارات خطة تدبير كاملة موثوقة.
clinicalPearl: An uncertain answer key must not override the source explanation that cautions against routine magic mouthwash.
sourceExplanationEn:
Primary herpetic gingivostomatitis is characterized by ulcerative lesions of the gingiva and mucous 
membranes of the mouth (picture 1), often with perioral vesicular lesions. It generally begins with a 
prodrome that lasts approximately four days and may in clude fever, anorexia, irritability, malaise, 
sleeplessness, and headache. Caregivers may attribute these symptoms to teething in children whose 
primary teeth are erupting, but children who are teething do not have oropharyngeal lesions. Associated 
symptoms and signs may include bad breath, refusal to drink, anorexia, fever, arthralgia, headache, and 
submandibular or cervical lymphadenitis. Refusal to drink may result in dehydration, which is the most 
frequent complication. [UpToDate] 
 
We do not routinely suggest "magic mouthwash" to coat lesions and/or soothe pain given the lack of 
evidence of benefit from clinical trials, the potential for harm (e.g., toxicity from systemic absorption, 
allergic reaction), and difficulty of application in young children. [UpToDate]

tts.text: A child who’s known to have Crohn's disease on infliximab presented with new onset vesicular skin rash on posterior rip distribution that is itching and associated with burning sensation. What would you do next? Option A. Give IV acyclovir. Option B. Give IV valganciclovir. Option C. Give Oral Augmentin.

scenarioAr: طفل لديه Crohn disease ويستخدم infliximab، وظهر طفح vesicular حاكّ وحارق بتوزع posterior rib؛ المطلوب الخطوة التالية.
explanationAr: المفتاح A: IV acyclovir. يصف المصدر VZV reactivation كطفح vesicular أحادي الجانب ضمن sensory-nerve distribution، ويذكر أن immunocompromised patients أكثر عرضة للنكس. الجداول المرفقة هنا صور شرح فقط، وليست صورًا سريرية كانت مطلوبة في السؤال. لم تُضف جرعة علاج جديدة.
incorrectOptionsAr: B وC: المصدر يحدد acyclovir للحالة الموصوفة ولا يوصي فيهما. أبقيت عبارة IV valganciclovir كما طُبعت للتدقيق، دون تصحيح صامت أوتقديمها كنظام علاجي مقبول.
clinicalPearl: The source connects immunosuppression plus a dermatomal vesicular eruption with VZV reactivation.
sourceExplanationEn:
Varicella zoster (shingles) results from reactivation of dormant virus. Since this occurs several years after 
the initial infection, herpes zoster is rarely seen in children. The disease manifests as a localized, one-sided 
vesicular rash, usually restricted to the skin distribution of a single sensory nerve. It is most often seen on 
the trunk, face, or head, and less frequently on the limbs. Vesicles resembling chickenpox appear in this 
delimited area, and progress and coalesce. The person may have pain, itching, and hyperesthesia. The acute 
skin lesions of herpes zoster subside by crusting in about 2 weeks. The most troublesome manifestation is 
postherpetic neuralgia, which causes persistent pain and discomfort. Herpes zoster can be treated with 
acyclovir (IV, 30 mg/ kg/day in three divided doses). [IAP Textbook of Pediatric Infectious Diseases 2023] 
 
Immunocompromised patients are at increased risk of Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) reactivation because of 
reduced T cell -mediated immunity. This includes transplant recipients, patients receiving selected 
immunomodulator therapies, patients treated with che motherapy and/or corticosteroids, and patients with 
human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). [UpToDate]

tts.text: A girl presented with asymptomatic perianal warts. What will you do next? Option A. Take detailed history. Option B. Reassure.

scenarioAr: طفلة لديها asymptomatic perianal warts؛ المطلوب الخطوة التالية.
explanationAr: المفتاح A: Take detailed history. يوضح المصدر أن HPV قد ينتقل بطرق غير جنسية، منها autoinoculation وheteroinoculation، وأن احتمال sexual abuse يستحق النظر ضمن التقييم. وجود الثآليل وحده لا يثبت الاعتداء، كما أن reassurance وحدها لا تستبدل أخذ التاريخ والتقييم.
incorrectOptionsAr: B: reassurance دون detailed history تتجاوز خطوة التقييم التي اختارها المصدر؛ لا يُفترض نمط انتقال بعينه من الآفات وحدها.
clinicalPearl: Perianal warts warrant a careful history; the source acknowledges both nonsexual transmission and safeguarding concerns.
sourceExplanationEn:
The child described in the vignette has condylomata acuminata (genital warts) as a result of human 
papillomavirus (HPV) infection. These lesions often present as 1 to 5 mm flesh-colored, verrucous papules, 
which may coalesce into large plaques. While children can potentially autoinoculate (spread of HPV from 
other sites on the patient) or heteroinoculate (spread by nonsexual contact with lesions of a caregiver or 
others), condylomata acuminata have been associated with childhood sexual abuse. Therefore, 

consideration of sexual abuse is warranted in the evaluation of the prepubescent child in this vignette.  
[Question 62 in PREP 2016]

Gram stain of the lesions came negative for any growth. What is the most likely cause? Option A. Herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection. Option B. Pustular melanosis. Option C. Fungal folliculitis.

image.captionAr: صورة السؤال الأصلية من الملف المرفوع؛ ليست تشخيصًا معتمدًا.
image.captionEn: Original source question image; independent clinical review pending.

scenarioAr: مراهقة ساءت آفات acne لديها مع itching بعد topical antibiotic؛ الصورة مرفقة ويذكر النص Gram stain سلبيًا؛ المطلوب السبب.
explanationAr: المفتاح C: Fungal folliculitis. يشرح المصدر أن Pityrosporum/Malassezia folliculitis تسبب papules وpustules حاكّة في مناطق غنية بالزهم، وقد تُخطأ باعتبارها acne ولا تتحسن مع antibiotics. عبارة Gram stain negative for any growth غير دقيقة في الأصل؛ حُفظت كما هي ووُسمت للمراجعة، ولم تُحوَّل إلى نتيجة culture مخترعة.
incorrectOptionsAr: A وB: لا يقدم المصدر مقارنة تفصيلية معهما؛ ترجيحه لـC مبني على pruritus والمظهر acneiform وعدم الاستجابة لعلاج acne المعتاد. النتيجة السلبية المذكورة لا تؤكد الفطريات وحدها.
clinicalPearl: Pruritic acneiform lesions resistant to conventional acne therapy prompt consideration of Malassezia folliculitis in the source.
sourceExplanationEn:
Pityrosporum folliculitis (PF) is fungal acneiform disease of the hair follicles that presents with papules 
and pustules often associated with pruritus. PF lesions most commonly present on the chest, shoulders, 
back or face most often appear during the second and third decades of life. PF and acne vulgaris have very 
similar presentations, and PF is often misdiagnosed as acne vulgaris (AV). Malassezia spp. fungi require a 
lipid source for survival and reproduction which leads these species to overgrow in sebum-rich areas of the 
body, where AV often occurs. Both PF and AV can present with papules and pustules and occur in similar 
locations across the body: face, chest, and back. Patients with PF are often incorrectly managed with 
traditional AV treatments, such as antibiotics, with little to no improvement. Thus, in cases of AV resistant 
to traditional management strategies, the diagnosis of PF should be considered. [Clinical characteristics and 
treatment outcomes of Pityrosporum folliculitis in immunocompetent patients]

tts.text: A child presented with band of hair loss with no scaring (alopecia areata case). What will you do for her? Option A. Reassurance. Option B. Oral griseofulvin. Option C. Topical griseofulvin.

scenarioAr: طفل لديه band of hair loss دون scarring ويسمي النص الحالة alopecia areata؛ المطلوب التدبير.
explanationAr: المفتاح A: Reassurance. الشرح المرجعي يضيف أن البقعة صغيرة وتتحسن وأن scalp طبيعي، وهي تفاصيل ليست مكتملة في الـstem المختصر. لذلك لا تُعمم reassurance على كل alopecia areata؛ بقيت الحاجة لتأكيد السياق واضحة.
incorrectOptionsAr: B وC: المصدر لا يرى دليل tinea capitis عند غياب scale وinflammation وblack-dot hairs، ولذلك لا يختار griseofulvin. هذه علامات من الشرح المرجعي ولا تُضاف كوقائع غير مذكورة إلى الـstem.
clinicalPearl: The reassurance answer is tied to a small improving alopecia-areata patch in the source explanation.
sourceExplanationEn:
The girl in the vignette has a round patch of nearly complete hair loss and a normal-appearing scalp. These 
findings suggest the diagnosis of alopecia areata. Since the patch is small and improving, no therapy is 
necessary. In the absence of scale, evidenc e of inflammation (erythema or pustule formation), or “black -

dot” hairs (the remnants of broken hairs within follicles), tinea capitis is unlikely and antifungal therapy is 
not indicated. [Question 62 in PREP 2016] 
 
For more information, please read the following [Hair Loss - AAP]

tts.text: A child presented with areas of hair loss. On examinations, black dots were seen at hair follicles (tinea capitis case). Which of the following is true regarding his condition? Option A. Topical treatment is enough. Option B. The cause is direct contact with infected animal or person. Option C. All contacts need to be treated.

scenarioAr: طفل لديه hair loss مع black dots عند hair follicles؛ المطلوب العبارة الصحيحة.
explanationAr: المفتاح B: direct contact with infected animal or person. يشرح المصدر أيضًا إمكان الانتقال عبر أدوات ملوثة. يحتاج tinea capitis إلى oral antifungal لأن topical therapy لا تصل جيدًا إلى hair follicles. يُفحص أفراد المنزل ويُعالج المصاب، ويذكر الشرح antifungal shampoo للمخالطين؛ وهذا غير إعطاء علاج فموي لكل شخص تلقائيًا.
incorrectOptionsAr: A: يخالف حاجة الإصابة داخل hair follicles إلى systemic treatment بحسب الشرح. C: صياغة all contacts need to be treated أوسع من التفصيل الوارد؛ المصدر يفرق بين علاج الإصابة المثبتة واستخدام shampoo للمخالطين.
clinicalPearl: Distinguish treatment of proven tinea capitis from preventive shampoo use for household contacts.
sourceExplanationEn:
Tinea capitis primarily occurs in children. The most common clinical findings are single or multiple scaly 
patches with alopecia and patches of alopecia with black dots at follicular orifices that represent broken 
hairs. Other presentations include widespr ead scaling with subtle hair loss, a boggy edematous painful 
plaque called a kerion, and favus, which characteristically exhibits multiple cup -shaped, yellow crusts 
(scutula). [UpToDate] 
 
Tinea capitis is acquired through contact of the scalp with the causative dermatophyte. Acquisition of the 
fungus may result from direct contact with an infected individual or animal or from contact with a 
contaminated object (e.g., comb, brush, or hat). [UpToDate] 
 
Treatment should involve an oral antifungal agent that has demonstrated efficacy for tinea capitis. Topical 
antifungal therapy is unlikely to be effective because topical treatments have inadequate penetration of hair 
follicles and may miss sites of subcli nical infection. Griseofulvin has a long history of use for childhood 
tinea capitis and is a well-accepted first-line therapy. [UpToDate] 
 
Household members of an individual diagnosed with tinea capitis should be physically examined for signs 
of tinea capitis and should be treated simultaneously if tinea capitis is detected. Asymptomatic carriers of 
dermatophytes may serve as reservoirs for r ecurrent infection. Because of this possibility, we suggest use 
of an antifungal shampoo by all household members for two to four weeks. [UpToDate]

image.captionAr: صورة السؤال الأصلية من الملف المرفوع؛ ليست تشخيصًا معتمدًا.
image.captionEn: Original source question image; independent clinical review pending.

scenarioAr: طفل لديه مناطق hair loss وحكة وصورة يُشار إليها كـtinea capitis أوkerion؛ المطلوب العلاج.
explanationAr: المفتاح A: Oral griseofulvin. يشرح المصدر أن oral antifungal هو أساس علاج tinea capitis وkerion، وأن topical therapy وحدها غير كافية. الصورة الوحيدة المتاحة لهذا السؤال في صفحة 647 رسم سريري مقارن ضمن الشرح، ويحمل أسماء التشخيصات؛ استُخرجت للشرح ولم تُقدَّم كصورة امتحان خالية من الإجابة.
incorrectOptionsAr: B: topical miconazole وحده لا يحقق اختراقًا كافيًا لـhair follicles بحسب المصدر. لا يثبت الشرح فائدة إضافة systemic glucocorticoid بصورة روتينية في kerion.
clinicalPearl: Use the labelled kerion/tinea image after answering; an unlabelled question image remains unavailable.
sourceExplanationEn:
The most common clinical manifestations of tinea capitis are the development of scaly patches with 
alopecia and patches of alopecia with visible black dots. Diffuse scalp scaling with subtle hair loss, kerion, 
and favus are additional clinical variants. Pr uritus is a common associated symptom in the various 
presentations of tinea capitis. Kerion is a severe manifestation of tinea capitis resulting from an intense 
immune response to the infection. Kerion is characterized by the development of an inflammatory  plaque 
with pustules, thick crusting, and/or drainage. A suppurative folliculitis may be the initial presentation. 
Tenderness or pain is often present. [UpToDate] 
 
Treatment should involve an oral antifungal agent that has demonstrated efficacy for tinea capitis. Topical 
antifungal therapy is unlikely to be effective because topical treatments have inadequate penetration of hair 
follicles and may miss sites of subcli nical infection. Griseofulvin has a long history of use for childhood 
tinea capitis and is a well-accepted first-line therapy. [UpToDate] 
 
Oral antifungal therapy is the mainstay of treatment for kerion. Treatment regimens are similar to treatment 
for other forms of tinea capitis. Systemic glucocorticoids are occasionally used in conjunction with 
antifungal therapy for patients with severe inflammation. However, it is unclear if the addition of a systemic 
glucocorticoid accelerates improvement or improves outcome. [UpToDate]

scenarioAr: طفل لديه itching بالرأس مع صورة head lice؛ المطلوب العلاج.
explanationAr: المفتاح A: Permethrin 1%. يذكر المصدر الاستعمال لمن أعمارهم شهران فأكثر وإعادة العلاج بعد 7–10 أيام، ويحذر من lindane بسبب السلامة. الفحص الخارجي المحدود من CDC مؤيد لهذه النقاط العامة، مع التنبيه إلى resistance وعدم تعميم ترتيب العلاج على كل منطقة أوكل حالة.
incorrectOptionsAr: B: المصدر لا يوصي بـlindane كخيار أول بسبب safety concerns. هذا السؤال يقارن خيارين محددين ولا يحصر جميع علاجات head lice المتاحة.
clinicalPearl: Keep 1% permethrin for head lice distinct from 5% permethrin used for scabies.
sourceExplanationEn:
Permethrin 1% cream rinse, available over the counter; first -line therapy; applied to hair that has been 
shampooed and towel dried; left on for 10 minutes and then rinsed; repeat treatment in 7 to 10 days; 
approved in infants 2 months and older. Topical li ndane is not recommended as a first -line treatment for 
pediculosis capitis because of safety concerns.

subtopic: Head lice contacts and school attendance
scenarioAr: أب لطفلة عمرها 6 سنوات شُخصت بـhead lice يسأل عن المخالطين والمدرسة وتوقيت إعادة العلاج.
explanationAr: المفتاح A يتعلق بمعالجة bedmates بالتزامن مع المصابين. المصدر يوصي بفحص household contacts، ويرفض no-nit policies، ويذكر أن إعادة permethrin تكون عادةً في اليوم التاسع وليس بعد 3–5 أيام. هذه التوصيات لا تعني علاج كل المخالطين عشوائيًا دون التفريق بين المصاب ومشارك السرير.
incorrectOptionsAr: B: يناقض موقف المصدر الذي يدعو إلى إلغاء no-nit policies. C: لا يطابق توقيت إعادة permethrin الذي يذكره المصدر، وهو عادةً day 9.
clinicalPearl: Treat affected individuals and bedmates together, and avoid unnecessary exclusion based on nits alone, as discussed in the source.
keywords: Head lice contacts and school attendance
sourceExplanationEn:
Treatment for head lice is recommended for persons diagnosed with an active infestation. All household 
members and other close contacts should be checked; those persons with evidence of an active infestation 
should be treated. Some experts believe prophylactic treatment is prudent for persons who share the same 
bed with actively-infested individuals. All infested persons (household members and close contacts) and 
their bedmates should be treated at the same time. [CDC]  
 
Permethrin may continue to kill newly hatched lice for several days after treatment. A second treatment 
often is necessary on day 9 to kill any newly hatched lice before they can produce new eggs. [CDC] 
 
Both the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and the National Association of School Nurses (NASN) 
advocate that “no-nit” policies should be discontinued. “No -nit” policies that require a child to be free of 
nits before they can return to schools should be discontinued for the following reasons: [CDC] 

• Many nits are more than ¼ inch from the scalp. Such nits are usually not viable and very unlikely 
to hatch to become crawling lice, or may in fact be empty shells, also known as ‘casings’. 
• Nits are cemented to hair shafts and are very unlikely to be transferred successfully to other people. 
• The burden of unnecessary absenteeism to the students, families and communities far outweighs the 
risks associated with head lice. 
• Misdiagnosis of nits is very common during nit checks conducted by nonmedical personnel.

image.captionAr: صورة السؤال الأصلية من الملف المرفوع؛ ليست تشخيصًا معتمدًا.

scenarioAr: رضيع عمره 6 أشهر لديه طفح حاكّ مع إصابة أحد إخوته وصور skin scraping؛ المطلوب العلاج.
explanationAr: المفتاح A: Ivermectin، لكن المصدر نفسه يقول إن permethrin سيكون الاختيار لو وُجد، وينبه إلى عدم ثبوت أمان ivermectin لمن يقل وزنهم عن 15 kg. لم يحدد الخيار route أوالوزن. لذلك بقي السؤال conflicting وغير صالح لاعتماد إجابة علاجية نهائية؛ لا يُفسَّر المفتاح كوصفة لرضيع.
incorrectOptionsAr: B: لا يقدم المصدر lindane كبديل مفضل وآمن لهذا العمر. C: Nizoral shampoo ليس الاختيار الذي يحدده شرح scabies. A: لا يمكن اعتماده دون route وweight ومراجعة السلامة؛ الخيار الأنسب الذي يناقشه المصدر غير موجود.
clinicalPearl: Do not turn a flawed infant-scabies option set into a verified ivermectin recommendation.
sourceExplanationEn:
Given its high efficacy and safety, permethrin is our preferred therapy for children. However, topical sulfur, 
which is considered safe in infants, is typically used for the treatment of infants under the age of two months 
because of lack of regulatory app roval for permethrin use in infants in this age group. Single -dose 
ivermectin (200 mcg/kg per dose) has been used (off -label) for crusted scabies or disease in 
immunocompromised patients; its safety in children weighing less than 15 kg has not been establi shed. 
Topical ivermectin is reportedly effective.
